title: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
authors: Akira Sone, Akram Touil, Emery Doucet, Sebastian Deffner
abstract: We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.
summary: This paper compares two methods for calculating quantum work statistics—One-Time (OTM) and Two-Time (TTM)—by testing their consistency against the symmetry of entanglement. The authors prove that the OTM scheme is fundamentally more consistent, as its results naturally follow from entanglement symmetry for all processes. Conversely, the TTM scheme is shown to be mathematically flawed, only yielding correct results for an infinitesimally small set of driving unitaries.
main_problem: The paper compares the consistency of quantum work statistics derived from two measurement schemes: the standard Two-Time Measurement (TTM) and the One-Time Measurement (OTM), using entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance) as the guiding symmetry.
main_result: The OTM scheme yields work statistics naturally from envariance for all unitaries, whereas the TTM scheme only yields consistent results for a set of unitaries with zero Haar measure, indicating a fundamental flaw in the TTM approach.
method: The authors use theoretical derivations involving unitary time evolution, defining work distributions via state overlaps, and employing advanced mathematical tools like Haar measure analysis and concentration inequalities to rigorously compare the two schemes.
model_or_system: The system is a bipartite quantum system ($H = H_1 \otimes H_2$) undergoing unitary time evolution driven by time-dependent Hamiltonians. The analysis focuses on the work extracted during the process.
key_observables: Work distribution, overlap functions ($G_{w,w'}$), and the degree of orthogonality of the derived state components ($\langle\phi_w|\phi_{w'}angle$).
important_parameters: The driving unitary $U_	au$, the initial and final energy spectra ($E_n, E'_m$), and the entanglement-assisted invariance principle.
main_assumptions: The TTM approach neglects the energetic and informational costs of projective measurements. The mathematical proofs rely on properties of real analytic functions on compact manifolds and the use of Haar measure on $U(d)$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical setup and the two measurement schemes (OTM vs. TTM). It then rigorously analyzes the mathematical consistency of the TTM scheme, proving its failure for generic unitaries. Finally, it establishes the OTM scheme's superior consistency by linking its results directly to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical understanding of measurement processes in quantum thermodynamics, showing how fundamental symmetries (like envariance) can resolve ambiguities in defining physical observables like work, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.
